- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.2) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.2) or volatile, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.
- Model consistently overreacts to recent spikes (e.g., +5–10% in 1–2 days); apply smoothing: cap forecast rise at +5% from prior peak.
- Model underestimates mean-reversion periods; if 3–5 consecutive days show downward trend, add 0.5–1.5% upward bias to forecast.
- For 30-day horizon, model often misses late-cycle peaks; adjust last 5–7 days of forecast upward by 1–2% if sentiment is neutral or slightly positive.
- If sentiment history shows no clear trend (mostly 0.00), model tends to be flat; add 0.5–1.0% upward bias to avoid underestimating mean reversion.
